items.summary: Multiple consolidated cases involved patients suing health care providers for sharing health data through Meta Pixel tracking software embedded in patient portal websites. The providers removed the cases to federal court under the federal officer removal statute, claiming they were acting under the federal Health and Human Services Department when creating patient portals to comply with the Meaningful Use Program. The Court of Appeals affirmed remand to state court, holding that creating patient portals constitutes compliance with federal regulation rather than acting under the federal government.

items.summary: Jarvis Roberts, proceeding pro se, appealed dismissal of his civil action against state prosecutors, judges, police officers, and other officials alleging prosecutorial misconduct and constitutional violations related to pending criminal charges against him. The Third Circuit affirmed most dismissals but modified the judgment to make certain jurisdictional dismissals without prejudice rather than with prejudice. The court found that Roberts's complaints lacked sufficient factual allegations against some defendants and that other defendants were entitled to immunity.

items.summary: Grove purchased a life insurance policy in 1994 with $96,420 total investment; his account value dropped to $336.12 by January 2025 without prior notice. The Court of Appeals vacated the district court's dismissal of his negligence and breach of fiduciary duty claims, holding that the court should have considered whether Grove could have discovered his injury under the discovery rule before applying the statute of limitations. The court remanded for determination of whether Grove, exercising reasonable diligence, should have known of his injury and when he should have discovered it.

items.summary: Patel worked for VMware earning commissions; he began working on a $20 million deal with the NYC Department of Education in 2019, but the deal closed after VMware changed its commission terms in 2021. VMware applied a 300% cap to his commission, reducing it by approximately half, more than two years after he started the deal. The Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for VMware under New Jersey's Wage Payment Law, holding that commissions are earned when the fiscal year terms are in effect and the deal closes, not when work begins.

items.summary: 233rd Street Partnership sought Fifth Amendment compensation for a federal taking of a rail corridor through a Notice of Interim Trail Use. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration 50 CFR Part 679 [Docket No. 261015-0010] RIN 0648-BO22 Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Modify Groundfish Season Timing in the Bering Sea and Aleutia
items.summary: NMFS proposes two technical revisions to regulations for the opening and closing times of groundfish fisheries in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (BSAI) and Gulf of Alaska (GOA) management areas. First, this proposed rule would authorize NMFS to determine the opening and closing times for the sablefish Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) and Community Development Quota (CDQ) fishing season, taking into consideration the halibut IFQ/CDQ season set by the International Pacific Halibut Commission (IPHC). Second, this proposed rule would allow NMFS flexibility to change the time of day for closing a groundfish fishery. This proposed rule is necessary to minimize regulatory discards, reduce uncertainty for fishery participants, and enable fuller utilization and more precise limitation of allowable harvest. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish of the BSAI Management Area (BSAI FMP) and the Fishery Management Plan for the Groundfish Fisheries of the GOA (GOA FMP), and other applicable laws.
items.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Modify Groundfish Season Timing in the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands and Gulf of Alaska Groundfish Fisheries

The provision is unnecessarily duplicative of a similar provision contained in NCUA's Chartering and Field of Membership Manual (Manual), and is outdated, having been superseded by amendments to the Manual.

items.opening_verbatim: NATIONAL CREDIT UNION ADMINISTRATION 12 CFR Parts 702, 703, and 741 RIN 3133-AG21 Nonconforming Investment Special Reserve AGENCY: National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). ACTION: Proposed rule. SUMMARY: The NCUA Board (Board) is propos
items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is proposing to amend its regulations governing the requirements for federal share insurance. This action would remove the requirement for federally insured, state-chartered credit unions to establish a special reserve for certain investments that are beyond those authorized for federally chartered credit unions. The intended effect is to reduce unnecessary compliance and administrative burdens for state-chartered insured credit unions without diminishing the agency's ability to protect the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund.

items.opening_verbatim: NATIONAL CREDIT UNION ADMINISTRATION 12 CFR Part 745 RIN 3133-AG24 Notification to Members/Shareholders AGENCY: National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). ACTION: Proposed rule. SUMMARY: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a
items.summary: The NCUA Board (Board) solicits public comment on a proposal to streamline the methods a federally insured credit union (FICU) may use to provide its members with notice of share insurance coverage. The current regulation is overly prescriptive, mandating that a FICU make available hard copies of certain prescribed materials. While a FICU would still be required to provide notice to members, the proposed rule would defer to the FICU on the method used for such notification. Among other methods, a FICU may elect to provide members with a link to updated online resources that will be maintained on the NCUA website. The Board believes the proposed rule will provide greater flexibility, reduce compliance costs for both NCUA and FICUs, and ensure that members are provided with up-to-date information regarding share insurance coverage.
items.title: Notification to Members/Shareholders

items.summary: Executive Order 14436 establishes tariff increases on Russian Federation goods and monitoring requirements pursuant to the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The order increases duties on Russian goods by 500 percent and on major crude oil and natural gas importers from Russia by 100 percent contingent on new purchases after October 18, 2026.
